issues.description: Method return-type mismatch for Milkable.messageOnMilk(): The problem statement (UML) declares Milkable.messageOnMilk() as returning boolean, but the solution repository defines the interface method as returning String and the concrete implementations (Seal, Goat) return String messages. The template Main also prints the result of messageOnMilk() as if it were a printable string. This cross-artifact inconsistency will confuse students about which return type to implement and may lead to incompatible implementations or failing tests.
issues.suggestedFix:
Pick one consistent return type for Milkable.messageOnMilk() across the UML/problem text, template code, and solution. Two viable options:
1) If the intended behavior is to produce a human-readable message (as in the solution), update the problem statement/UML to declare messageOnMilk(): String, and keep the solution Main printing the returned string. Update any tests/documentation to expect the String message (e.g., "<AnimalType> <name> is milked").
2) If the intended behavior is a boolean success flag (as the UML currently states), change the solution interface and implementations to return boolean, update Seal/Goat implementations accordingly, and adjust any code that prints the result (e.g., print a message based on the boolean). Ensure the template Main and tests are updated to match the chosen signature.
